links.targetTitle: The Loss Given Default formula as written in the Atlas alway

title: The reference implementation clamps Loss Given Default to [0,1], confirming the published formula's bound is written backwards
content:
A.3.2.2.1.1.1.1.1.2 states the Loss Given Default step as `LGD = min(1 - (1 - LP) * (1 - S) / LT, 0)`, which can never return a positive number and would zero out every capital requirement downstream.

The reference implementation included at A.3.2.2.1.1.1.1.5 settles the question of intent. It computes recovery as a share-weighted sum across collateral positions of `(1 - liquidation_penalty) * (1 - slippage) / liquidation_threshold`, then applies `lgd = max(0.0, min(1 - recovery, 1.0))`.

So the intended semantics are a two-sided clamp of the loss fraction to the unit interval: floor at 0 when recovery exceeds the debt, cap at 1 when recovery is worthless. The prose's `min(..., 0)` is a transposition of the floor.

Two consequences follow. First, the defect is confined to the prose and does not affect anything computed from the reference code — but the Atlas is the normative artifact, so an independent implementer following only the specification would produce a framework that requires zero capital. Second, the code makes a modelling choice the prose does not state: recovery is aggregated **across positions** as a share-weighted average before the clamp, so an over-collateralized position can offset an under-recovering one within the same Instance, rather than each position being floored independently.
description: Prose gives LGD = min(1 − recovery, 0); the code computes max(0.0, min(1 − recovery, 1.0)) — resolving the defect and making the code, not the formula, the operative definition.
